text.content:
Floralists identify and cultivate the strange seeds grown from the spiritual energy that flows within plants.

SKILLS

CHLOROMANCY · SL max 10

Each level discovers one magiseed type. In a conflict, if your garden is empty: action + 20 MP plants a magiseed you have discovered.

BATTLE GARDENING · SL max 3

After planting through Chloromancy (not Graft), choose one: a free attack with an equipped weapon, or the Spell action for free casting a spell of (5 + SL × 5) MP or less (you still pay it). High Roll treated as 0 either way.

GRAFT · SL max 1

With a magiseed in your garden and 1+ Growth Clock sections filled, action: swap it for a different magiseed you have discovered, keeping the filled sections unchanged.

TREE OF LIFE · SL max 5

When a magiseed is removed from your garden, one creature you can see that is in Crisis recovers (5 + SL × 5) HP.

VERDANT SWAY · SL max 1

Grants Rituals of the Ritualism discipline, extended to creating, animating and controlling vegetation, pollen, spores and toxins — never plant-Species NPCs. Runs under the standing rulings that keep it inside the benefit-pool architecture.

pages.name: THE GARDEN AND THE GROWTH CLOCK

text.content:
The garden is an abstract space whose look depends on the character — a pot on their back, a gap along their blade, the ground under their feet.

  • It holds one magiseed at a time.
  • Any magiseed in your garden is removed automatically at the end of each scene.

The Growth Clock arrives with the Chloromancy Skill and is present only during conflict scenes.

  • 4 sections. It begins each scene empty.
  • At the end of your turn, if a magiseed is in your garden, fill 1 section. Then, if the magiseed is still there and has an "at the end of your turn" effect, apply that effect.
  • When you fill the fourth section, remove the magiseed, then erase all sections.
  • Sections may not be filled or erased by any other means — only as above, through Brambleheart and Green Thumb, or through effects that explicitly affect Growth Clocks.

Magiseed effects are keyed to the exact number of filled sections (T). You apply only the tier matching the current count — never the tiers below or above it.

Scaling: a magiseed effect that deals damage deals 5 extra at level 30 or higher. A magiseed effect causing HP and/or MP loss or recovery increases that amount by 10 at level 30 or higher.

Twenty standard magiseeds. Your group may also invent new ones collaboratively, and the GM may hand them out as rewards independently of Chloromancy investment; each is worth roughly 1000 zenit, and new ones should sit at a similar power to the standard list.

Defensive seeds

MagiseedTEffect
Arctic Narcissus0–1You are Resistant to earth and ice
2–3You and your allies present on the scene are Resistant to earth and ice
Desert Dahlia0–1You are Resistant to air and fire
2–3You and your allies present on the scene are Resistant to air and fire
Horned Hawthorn0–1You are Resistant to dark and poison
2–3You and your allies present on the scene are Resistant to dark and poison
Silver Strelitzia0–1You are Resistant to bolt and light
2–3You and your allies present on the scene are Resistant to bolt and light
Wardwattle0–1You are Resistant to physical
2Resistant to physical; after a creature hits you with a melee attack, deal (5 + your SL in Chloromancy) physical damage to it, after their attack resolves
3As tier 2, and then deal (5 + your SL in Chloromancy) poison damage to it as well — both after their attack resolves

Type-forcing seeds

MagiseedTEffect
Blazing Chrysanthemum1–3At the end of your turn, choose earth or fire. Until you use this effect again or the seed leaves your garden, all damage dealt by you and every ally present on the scene becomes that type, its type cannot change, and it ignores Resistances
Lunar Magnolia1–3As above, choosing ice or light
Prancing Dandelion1–3As above, choosing air or bolt
Hookleaf Nightshade0–1All damage you deal becomes poison, its type cannot change, and it ignores Resistances and Immunities
2–3As tier 0–1, and the first time you deal poison damage during your turn you deal extra damage equal to (your SL in Chloromancy); each creature that lost HP this way suffers poisoned

Status and damage seeds

MagiseedTEffect
Grave Asphodel1At the end of your turn you may choose an enemy you can see: they suffer shaken
2At the end of your turn, every enemy you can see suffers shaken
3At the end of your turn, deal (15 + your SL in Chloromancy) dark damage to each enemy you can see who is shaken
Serrated Rose1 / 2 / 3Same shape with slow, dealing (15 + SL) physical at tier 3
Star Peony1 / 2 / 3Same shape with dazed, dealing (15 + SL) light at tier 3
Striped Orchid1 / 2 / 3Same shape with weak, dealing (15 + SL) poison at tier 3

Support seeds

MagiseedTEffect
Golden Ginkgo1At the end of your turn, you and every ally you can see recover from dazed, enraged and shaken
2–3At the end of your turn, you and every ally you can see recover (5 + your SL in Chloromancy) Mind Points
Remedy Lily1At the end of your turn, you and every ally you can see recover from poisoned, slow and weak
2–3At the end of your turn, you and every ally you can see recover (15 + your SL in Chloromancy) Hit Points
Pilgrim Gazalia1–2At the end of your turn, choose yourself or another PC you can see: they regain 2 Inventory Points
3At the end of your turn, you and every other PC you can see regain 1 Inventory Point

Attribute and immunity seeds

MagiseedTEffect
Ocean Lotus0–1You are immune to dazed and slow
2You treat Dexterity and Insight as one die size higher, max d12
3You and every ally you can see treat Dexterity and Insight as one die size higher, max d12
Regal Protea0–1You are immune to shaken and weak
2You treat Might and Willpower as one die size higher, max d12
3You and every ally you can see treat Might and Willpower as one die size higher, max d12

Ocean Lotus and Regal Protea at tiers 2–3 count against the two-effect cap, and at tier 3 they hand the die increase to the whole party. This stacking has been flagged and not ruled — ask your GM.

The intelligence seed

MagiseedTEffect
Hermit Iris1At the end of your turn, choose an enemy you can see. The GM reveals its Level, Rank, Species, maximum HP, maximum MP, Traits, Attributes, Defense and Magic Defense
2–3As tier 1, plus Affinities and pressure points

The odd one out

MagiseedTEffect
Wrathful Carnation1–4When this magiseed leaves your garden, choose up to one enemy you can see: until the end of your next turn, when that enemy attacks or casts an offensive spell they must include you among the targets, if able. And: at the end of your turn you may remove this magiseed from your garden; if you do, erase all sections of your Growth Clock
